analysis.title: GS Chryssafis - 10 Charts We're Talking About 5 Nov 2026
key_insights: Equities took the midterm results in stride. The better-than-expected Democratic result and JD Vance's tweet are read as implying more guardrails on the Iran war, some rollback of select tariffs and a reversal of recently enacted spending cuts.
Historically a divided government has been one of the best post-election combinations for equities, particularly over a 3-6 month period.
Equity enthusiasm was not uniform. Tech is showing weakness again on the morning of 5 Nov.

GS strategists note that Democratic wins at the state and local level have significant implications for AI and data center regulation, which could hurt select US utilities and Independent Power Producers. GS expects the data center issue to fade in importance and any moratoria to be short-lived.

Global investors worried about over-indexation to US tech are expected to keep diversifying, either within US equities or into non-US AI beneficiaries. October's outperformance of value relative to growth was the largest since 1990.
CSI300, seen as a China hardware tech proxy, is up 3% month to date after its worst month in a decade (-8.5% in October).
The GSPUCHAI Index (long China AI vs short US AI) rose almost 10% overnight, as any slowdown in US AI development is seen as a relative gain for China.
The reduction in Iran risk premium has renewed interest in gold. Privo argues long gold may be a more defensible de-escalation trade than short oil, given how much premium has already come out.
GS's CTA model is close to max short in gold, and GS thinks the pain trade is ultimately higher.

CTAs should also be sellers in oil, but the bounce off the 100d/200dma is notable. GS is watching US-Iran negotiation headlines as the '36hrs' Qatar cited on Tuesday expires. Without progress GS expects some return of risk premium, but a return to significant escalation is much less likely after the midterms.

GS hopes for continued easing of global supply chain stress, which has kept supply-driven inflation elevated, in order to ease financial conditions. Otherwise the market will struggle to handicap the extent of a hiking cycle, particularly with US growth surprising to the upside.
The labor market remains relatively robust. Initial jobless claims were soft again and the seasonally adjusted 4-week average is the lowest since 1969.
There is a disconnect between the outright level of the USD and USD positioning. GS sees USD call vol, which is cheap on an outright basis, as attractive for hedges.

sector_views.rationale: Democratic state and local wins could bring AI and data center regulation that hurts select US utilities and IPPs, but GS expects the issue to fade and any moratoria to be short-lived.
Value outperformed growth in October by the largest margin since 1990, and diversification away from US tech is expected to continue.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Labor market is relatively robust. Claims were soft again today, which supports the US growth surprise and hiking-risk narrative.
Worst month in a decade. The index has bounced 3% month to date.
Evidence of rotation away from US growth and tech within US equities.

trade_ideas.description: Long USD call vol as a hedge
trade_ideas.rationale: USD call vol remains cheap on an outright basis, and USD positioning is disconnected from the outright level.

trade_ideas.description: Long gold as a de-escalation trade, preferred over short oil (Privo, quoted by GS)
trade_ideas.rationale: Central banks stop buying or sell gold under higher energy bills, and as oil reverses, funding pressure eases and gold catches a bid. GS's CTA model is close to max short, so the pain trade is higher.

risk_factors: US-Iran negotiations stall after the '36hrs' window expires, bringing back some risk premium.
Global supply chain stress fails to ease, keeping supply-driven inflation elevated and making the extent of a hiking cycle hard to price.
Democratic state and local wins lead to AI and data center regulation or moratoria that hurt US utilities and IPPs.
Continued weakness in US tech as investors diversify.
